weekSubtitle: Estimating Length (in vs ft), Measuring with Rulers (cm), and Comparing Heights & Meters

practices.title: Practice 1: 📏 Estimating Length (Inches vs. Feet)
practices.description: Estimate real-world objects: books, doors, cups, cars, pianos, school buses, suitcases, and animals in inches and feet!
practices.hint: Remember: An inch is small like a paperclip or thumb tip. A foot is 12 inches, like a classroom ruler!

practices.title: Practice 2: 📐 Measuring with Rulers (Centimeters • cm)
practices.description: Use the centimeter ruler to measure lines, pencils, blocks, crayons, scissors, and erasers accurately!
practices.hint: Always line up the start of the object with 0 on the ruler, then read the number at the other end!

practices.title: Practice 3: ⚖️ Comparing Lengths & Heights (Meters & Differences)
practices.description: Compare trees, cars, and trucks in meters. Identify shortest and longest, and subtract to find differences!
practices.hint: To find how much longer, taller, or shorter, subtract the smaller length from the larger length!

quiz.title: Revision Final Quiz: Measuring Master Challenge
quiz.description: A 10-question challenge testing length estimation, centimeter ruler readings, and comparing meters!
quiz.hint: Look closely at the rulers, read the numbers at each end, and calculate step-by-step!
quiz.instruction: Look at the picture or read the question, then tap the best answer!

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of the book. Which gives the best estimate?
questions.speechText: A reading book is about 1 foot or 1 inch?
questions.hint: An inch is tiny like a paperclip. A foot is 12 inches, like a standard school ruler!
questions.explanation: A book is about 1 foot long (12 inches). 1 inch is much too small!

measuringVisual.name: Reading Book
measuringVisual.categoryHint: About the length of a classroom ruler

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a house door. Which gives the best estimate?
questions.speechText: A house door is about 7 feet or 7 inches?
questions.hint: An adult person can walk through a door. A grown-up is around 5 to 6 feet tall!
questions.explanation: A house door is about 7 feet tall so tall adults can walk through easily.

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a coffee mug. Which gives the best estimate?
questions.speechText: A coffee mug is about 3 inches or 3 feet?
questions.hint: You can hold a mug in one hand. 3 feet would be as tall as a kitchen table!
questions.explanation: A coffee mug is about 3 inches tall. 3 feet would be giant!

measuringVisual.name: Coffee Mug
measuringVisual.categoryHint: Small enough to hold in your hand

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a car. Which gives the best estimate?
questions.speechText: A family car is about 10 feet or 10 inches?
questions.hint: A car fits several people inside. 10 inches is smaller than a ruler!
questions.explanation: A real family car is about 10 to 15 feet long. 10 inches would be a toy car!

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a room window. Which gives the best estimate?
questions.speechText: A room window is about 5 feet or 5 inches?
questions.hint: A window on the wall is almost as tall as an adult! 5 inches is tiny.
questions.explanation: A room window is about 5 feet tall. 5 inches is smaller than a pencil!

measuringVisual.name: Room Window
measuringVisual.categoryHint: On the wall of a house

questions.prompt: Estimate the width of a baseball. Which gives the best estimate?
questions.speechText: A baseball is about 4 inches or 4 feet?
questions.hint: A baseball fits in your palm. 4 feet would be as wide as a desk!
questions.explanation: A baseball is about 3 to 4 inches across so a pitcher can hold and throw it.

measuringVisual.name: Baseball
measuringVisual.categoryHint: Fits inside your glove or hand

questions.prompt: Estimate the width of a grand piano. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A grand piano is about 58 inches or 58 feet?
questions.hint: 58 inches is almost 5 feet. 58 feet would be longer than a house!
questions.explanation: A grand piano is about 58 inches wide (nearly 5 feet). 58 feet would be giant!

measuringVisual.name: Grand Piano
measuringVisual.categoryHint: Musical instrument in a concert hall

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a school bus. Check the correct option:
questions.text: A yellow school bus is about:
questions.speechText: A yellow school bus is about 42 feet or 42 inches?
questions.hint: A bus carries dozens of children. 42 inches is only 3.5 feet, shorter than a 2nd grader!
questions.explanation: A full-size school bus is about 42 feet long to seat many students.

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a cardboard box. Check the correct option:
questions.text: A shipping cardboard box is about:
questions.speechText: A shipping cardboard box is about 18 inches or 18 feet?
questions.hint: 18 inches is 1 and a half feet. 18 feet is as tall as a two-story building!
questions.explanation: A cardboard delivery box is about 18 inches tall. 18 feet would be massive!

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a travel suitcase. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A travel suitcase is about 24 inches or 24 feet?
questions.hint: 24 inches is exactly 2 feet. 24 feet is as long as two cars combined!
questions.explanation: A standard luggage suitcase is about 24 inches long (2 feet) to pack clothes.

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a small step ladder. Check the correct option:
questions.text: A household step stool ladder is about:
questions.speechText: A household step stool ladder is about 30 inches or 30 feet?
questions.hint: 30 inches is 2.5 feet, reaching high kitchen shelves. 30 feet is for fire trucks!
questions.explanation: A small kitchen step ladder is about 30 inches tall (2 and a half feet).

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of an ice popsicle. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: An ice popsicle is about 3 inches or 3 feet?
questions.hint: You hold a popsicle by its wooden stick. 3 feet would be as long as a baseball bat!
questions.explanation: A popsicle treat is about 3 inches long. 3 feet would be impossible to hold!

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a fresh carrot. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A garden carrot is about 6 inches or 6 feet?
questions.hint: A carrot is about half the length of a ruler (6 inches). 6 feet is as tall as a man!
questions.explanation: A garden carrot is about 6 inches long. 6 feet would be giant vegetable!

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of an African giraffe. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A tall giraffe is about 12 feet or 12 inches?
questions.hint: A giraffe has a super long neck that reaches high tree leaves! 12 inches is just 1 foot.
questions.explanation: A giraffe is about 12 to 18 feet tall! 12 inches would be tiny like a kitten.

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a notebook. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A school notebook is about 8 inches or 8 feet?
questions.hint: A notebook easily fits in your backpack. 8 feet would touch the ceiling!
questions.explanation: A school notebook is about 8 to 10 inches tall. 8 feet is as high as a room ceiling!

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a yellow banana. Check the correct option:
questions.text: A ripe yellow banana is about:
questions.speechText: A ripe yellow banana is about 6 inches or 6 feet?
questions.hint: You can hold a banana easily. 6 feet is taller than your teacher!
questions.explanation: A ripe banana is about 6 to 8 inches long. 6 feet would be as big as a human!

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a kitchen toaster. Check the correct option:
questions.text: A kitchen bread toaster is about:
questions.speechText: A kitchen bread toaster is about 15 inches or 15 feet?
questions.hint: A toaster sits neatly on the kitchen counter. 15 feet would cover the whole kitchen!
questions.explanation: A 2-slice or 4-slice toaster is about 12 to 15 inches long (just over 1 foot).

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a garden rake or broom. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A garden rake is about 2 feet or 2 inches?
questions.hint: A child garden rake or rake head is around 2 feet. 2 inches is small like a paperclip!
questions.explanation: A garden rake or broom is around 2 to 4 feet long so you can sweep leaves.

measuringVisual.name: Garden Rake
measuringVisual.categoryHint: Tool used to collect autumn leaves

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a brass saxophone. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A musical saxophone is about 25 inches or 25 feet?
questions.hint: A musician holds the saxophone in their lap. 25 feet is as long as a boat!
questions.explanation: An alto saxophone is about 25 inches long (about 2 feet).

questions.prompt: Estimate the length of a rescue helicopter. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A rescue helicopter is about 85 feet or 85 inches?
questions.hint: A helicopter carries pilots, doctors, and patients! 85 inches is only 7 feet, too small!
questions.explanation: A real helicopter is about 50 to 85 feet long from rotor to tail rotor.

measuringVisual.name: Rescue Helicopter
measuringVisual.categoryHint: Flies in the air to rescue people

questions.prompt: Estimate the height of a small cottage window. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: A square window is about 3 feet or 3 inches?
questions.hint: 3 feet is 36 inches (about 3 rulers). 3 inches is only as big as an eraser!
questions.explanation: A standard square cottage window is about 3 feet tall and 3 feet wide.

questions.prompt: Estimate the width of an autumn pumpkin. Check the correct option:
questions.speechText: An autumn pumpkin is about 12 inches or 12 feet?
questions.hint: 12 inches is exactly 1 foot, perfect to carve for Halloween! 12 feet is as tall as a house!
questions.explanation: A large pumpkin is about 12 inches wide (1 foot). 12 feet would be massive!

measuringVisual.name: Autumn Pumpkin
measuringVisual.categoryHint: Round orange pumpkin from the patch

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler and measure the black line in centimeters (cm):
questions.speechText: Look at the ruler. How many centimeters long is the line?
questions.hint: Check where the line starts (0) and where it ends on the ruler.
questions.explanation: The line starts at 0 cm and ends right at 14 cm. Its length is 14 cm!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler and measure the yellow pencil in centimeters (cm):
questions.speechText: Look at the ruler. How many centimeters long is the pencil?
questions.hint: The eraser is at 0. Follow the sharp tip down to the ruler mark.
questions.explanation: The pencil starts at 0 cm and its sharpened point reaches 13 cm. Length = 13 cm!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler and measure the blue building block in centimeters (cm):
questions.text: The blue block is ___ centimeters long.
questions.speechText: Look at the ruler. How many centimeters long is the blue block?
questions.hint: The block starts at 0. Look at the right edge of the blue block.
questions.explanation: The blue block starts at 0 cm and ends at 11 cm. Length = 11 cm!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler and measure the red crayon in centimeters (cm):
questions.text: The red crayon is ___ centimeters long.
questions.speechText: Look at the ruler. How many centimeters long is the red crayon?
questions.hint: The back of the crayon is at 0. Follow the pointed tip down to the ruler.
questions.explanation: The red crayon starts at 0 cm and points straight to 10 cm. Length = 10 cm!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler and measure the pink and blue eraser in centimeters (cm):
questions.speechText: Look at the ruler. How many centimeters long is the eraser?
questions.hint: Start at 0 on the left. The right edge of the eraser stops at 6.
questions.explanation: The eraser starts at 0 cm and ends at 6 cm. Length = 6 cm!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler comparing items. How long is the green crayon?
questions.speechText: How long is the crayon on the ruler?
questions.hint: Look at the green crayon at the top. The dotted line points to 7.
questions.explanation: The green crayon starts at 0 and ends at 7 cm. It is 7 centimeters long!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler comparing items. How long are the red scissors?
questions.speechText: How long are the scissors on the ruler?
questions.hint: The handles start at 0. Follow the tips of the blades down to the ruler.
questions.explanation: The scissors start at 0 and reach the 12 cm mark. They are 12 centimeters long!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler comparing items. How long is the glue stick?
questions.text: The glue stick is ___ centimeters long.
questions.speechText: How long is the glue stick on the ruler?
questions.hint: The bottom of the glue stick is at 0. The cap ends at 9.
questions.explanation: The glue stick starts at 0 and ends at 9 cm. It is 9 centimeters long!

questions.prompt: Ruler Measurement Rule: Where must you always start when measuring with a ruler?
questions.text: When measuring an object with a ruler, always line up the start with:
questions.speechText: When measuring an object with a ruler, always line up the start with what number?
questions.hint: Remember: Start at 0 on the ruler so you count the full length accurately!
questions.explanation: Always start at 0 on the ruler! If you start at 1, your measurement will be 1 cm too short.

questions.prompt: Understanding units: What does the abbreviation "cm" stand for on a classroom ruler?
questions.speechText: What does the abbreviation c m stand for on a ruler?
questions.hint: It is a metric unit for measuring smaller objects like pencils and erasers.
questions.explanation: "cm" stands for centimeters. There are 100 centimeters in 1 meter!

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler: An object starts at 0 cm and ends at 5 cm. How long is it?
questions.speechText: An object starts at 0 and ends at 5 centimeters. How long is it?
questions.hint: 5 - 0 = 5 centimeters.
questions.explanation: Starting at 0 and ending at 5 means the object is exactly 5 cm long.

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler: A marker starts at 0 cm and stops at 12 cm. How long is it?
questions.speechText: A marker starts at 0 and stops at 12 centimeters. How long is it?
questions.hint: Read the number where the tip ends: 12.
questions.explanation: The marker ends right on 12 cm, so its length is 12 centimeters.

questions.prompt: Look at Tree A (4 m) and Tree B (3 m). Which tree is taller?
questions.speechText: Tree A is 4 meters and Tree B is 3 meters. Which tree is taller?
questions.hint: Compare 4 meters and 3 meters. Which number is greater?
questions.explanation: Tree A is 4 meters tall, which is taller than Tree B (3 meters). 4 > 3!

questions.prompt: Look at Tree A (4 m) and Tree B (3 m). How much taller is Tree A than Tree B?
questions.text: Tree A is ___ meter taller than Tree B.
questions.speechText: How much taller is Tree A than Tree B?
questions.hint: Subtract: 4 m - 3 m = ?
questions.explanation: 4 m - 3 m = 1 m! Tree A is 1 meter taller than Tree B.

questions.prompt: Look at Car C (2 m) and Car D (3 m). Which car is longer?
questions.speechText: Car C is 2 meters and Car D is 3 meters. Which car is longer?
questions.hint: Compare 3 meters and 2 meters. Which is longer?
questions.explanation: Car D is 3 meters long, which is longer than Car C (2 meters). 3 > 2!

questions.prompt: Look at Car C (2 m) and Car D (3 m). How much longer is Car D than Car C?
questions.text: Car D is ___ meter longer than Car C.
questions.speechText: How much longer is Car D than Car C?
questions.hint: Subtract the lengths: 3 m - 2 m = ?
questions.explanation: 3 m - 2 m = 1 m! Car D is 1 meter longer than Car C.

questions.prompt: Look at Truck A (3 m), Truck B (4 m), and Truck C (6 m). Which truck is the shortest?
questions.speechText: Truck A is 3 meters, Truck B is 4 meters, and Truck C is 6 meters. Which truck is the shortest?
questions.hint: Look for the smallest number: 3 m, 4 m, or 6 m?
questions.explanation: Truck A is 3 meters long, which is the smallest length among the three trucks.

questions.prompt: Look at Truck A (3 m), Truck B (4 m), and Truck C (6 m). Which truck is the longest?
questions.speechText: Which truck is the longest?
questions.hint: Look for the greatest number: 3 m, 4 m, or 6 m?
questions.explanation: Truck C is 6 meters long, which makes it the longest truck.

questions.prompt: Look at Truck A (3 m) and Truck C (6 m). How many meters longer is Truck C than Truck A?
questions.text: Truck C is ___ meters longer than Truck A.
questions.speechText: Truck C is how many meters longer than Truck A?
questions.hint: Subtract: 6 m - 3 m = ?
questions.explanation: 6 m - 3 m = 3 meters! Truck C is 3 meters longer than Truck A.

questions.prompt: Look at Truck A (3 m) and Truck B (4 m). How many meters shorter is Truck A than Truck B?
questions.text: Truck A is ___ meter shorter than Truck B.
questions.speechText: Truck A is how many meters shorter than Truck B?
questions.hint: Subtract: 4 m - 3 m = ?
questions.explanation: 4 m - 3 m = 1 meter! Truck A is 1 meter shorter than Truck B.

questions.prompt: Look at Truck B (4 m) and Truck C (6 m). How many meters shorter is Truck B than Truck C?
questions.text: Truck B is ___ meters shorter than Truck C.
questions.speechText: Truck B is how many meters shorter than Truck C?
questions.hint: Subtract: 6 m - 4 m = ?
questions.explanation: 6 m - 4 m = 2 meters! Truck B is 2 meters shorter than Truck C.

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler with the crayon (7 cm), glue stick (9 cm), and scissors (12 cm). Which object is the shortest?
questions.speechText: The crayon is 7 cm, glue stick is 9 cm, and scissors are 12 cm. Which is the shortest object?
questions.hint: Compare 7 cm, 9 cm, and 12 cm. 7 is the smallest number!
questions.explanation: The crayon is 7 cm long, which is shorter than the glue stick (9 cm) and scissors (12 cm).

questions.prompt: Look at the ruler with the crayon (7 cm), glue stick (9 cm), and scissors (12 cm). Which object is the longest?
questions.speechText: Which is the longest object on the ruler?
questions.hint: Compare 7 cm, 9 cm, and 12 cm. 12 is the greatest number!
questions.explanation: The scissors reach all the way to 12 cm, making them the longest object.

questions.prompt: Look at the scissors (12 cm) and the crayon (7 cm). How much longer are the scissors than the crayon?
questions.text: The scissors are ___ centimeters longer than the crayon.
questions.speechText: How much longer are the scissors than the crayon?
questions.hint: Subtract the lengths: 12 cm - 7 cm = ?
questions.explanation: 12 cm - 7 cm = 5 cm! The scissors are 5 centimeters longer than the crayon.

questions.prompt: Look at the glue stick (9 cm) and the crayon (7 cm). How much longer is the glue stick than the crayon?
questions.text: The glue stick is ___ centimeters longer than the crayon.
questions.speechText: How much longer is the glue stick than the crayon?
questions.hint: Subtract the lengths: 9 cm - 7 cm = ?
questions.explanation: 9 cm - 7 cm = 2 cm! The glue stick is 2 centimeters longer than the crayon.

questions.prompt: Look at the glue stick (9 cm) and the scissors (12 cm). How much shorter is the glue stick than the scissors?
questions.text: The glue stick is ___ centimeters shorter than the scissors.
questions.speechText: How much shorter is the glue stick than the scissors?
questions.hint: Subtract: 12 cm - 9 cm = ?
questions.explanation: 12 cm - 9 cm = 3 cm! The glue stick is 3 centimeters shorter than the scissors.

questions.prompt: Combined lengths: If you park Truck A (3 m) and Truck B (4 m) back to back, what is their total length?
questions.text: Truck A (3 m) + Truck B (4 m) = ___ meters in all.
questions.speechText: What is 3 meters plus 4 meters?
questions.hint: Add the two lengths together: 3 + 4 = ?
questions.explanation: 3 m + 4 m = 7 meters! Combined they measure 7 meters in total.

questions.prompt: Height comparison: A sunflower is 2 meters tall. A corn stalk is 3 meters tall. How much taller is the corn stalk?
questions.text: The corn stalk is ___ meter taller than the sunflower.
questions.speechText: The corn stalk is 3 meters and the sunflower is 2 meters. How much taller is the corn stalk?
questions.hint: Subtract: 3 m - 2 m = ?
questions.explanation: 3 m - 2 m = 1 meter difference in height!
